title: How China Quietly Took Control of the Metals in Your Phone
hook: There's a tiny magnet inside your phone, your earbuds and your car. And almost every one of them passes through one country: China.
summary:
How did the whole world end up depending on one country for something this small? In this video we follow the story from a desert mine in California that once supplied most of the world, to the factory town of Baotou in China, a fight over a few empty islands in 2010, and the export licenses of 2025 that shut down a Ford factory in Chicago. Rare earths aren't actually rare. The hard part is separating them, and only one country was willing to do the dirty work.

Update: China's one-year pause on its newest rare earth rules runs until 10 November 2026. The licenses from April 2025 still apply.
